panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Panel A is a clinical photograph (retinography) showing pathology in the eye of a human patient, consistent with the diagnosis of presumed ocular histoplasmosis syndrome according to the article title and caption. B: Panel B is an early phase fluorescein angiogram (FA), which provides dynamic evidence of pathology consistent with POHS, specifically noting leakage. C: Panel C is a late phase fluorescein angiogram (FA), providing dynamic evidence of leakage consistent with active disease presentation of POHS.

plate_findings.evidence: peripapillary areas of hyper- and hypopigmentation
abnormal early hyperfluorescence in the fovea in the early frame

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels ((a), (b), (c), (d)). (a): Ulwide-field color photo showing peripapillary pigmentation changes and punched-out chorioretinal lesions, findings classic for POHS, as noted in the caption. (b): Ulwide-field color photo showing peripapillary pigmentation changes and punched-out chorioretinal lesions, findings classic for POHS, as noted in the caption. (c): 30-degree fluorescein angiography showing abnormal early hyperfluorescence in the fovea, consistent with neovascularization (CNV) in the context of POHS. (d): 30-degree fluorescein angiography showing intense leakage in the late frame, consistent with active choroidal neovascularization in the context of POHS.

panels.figure_caption: Ultra-wide-field color photographs of the right eye (a) and left eye (b) at presentation showing peripapillary areas of hyper- and hypopigmentation and punched-out chorioretinal lesions in the midperipheral retina, findings classic for presumed ocular histoplasmosis syndrome. 30-degree fluorescein angiography of the right eye showed abnormal early hyperfluorescence in the fovea in the early frame (c) and intense leakage in the late frame (d).
in_text_mentions: Dilated fundus examination of both eyes showed peripapillary hyper- and hypopigmentation and punched-out chorioretinal lesions in the midperipheral retina consistent with a diagnosis of POHS (Figures 1(a) and 1(b)). Additionally, the right eye showed foveal retinal thickening with trace subretinal hemorrhage and parafoveal intraretinal lipid. Fluorescein angiography (FA) of the right eye showed early hyperfluorescence in the fovea with intense leakage in the late frames, consistent with the presence of CNV (Figures 1(c) and 1(d)).
